build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player rolls a set of dice (at least 5) each combat turn with a tumble animation. Die faces show ability icons (sword, shield, heart, skull, etc.). Results land face-up and are clearly readable. Score 0 if no dice rolling exists.

After rolling, the player selects dice to keep (they lock in place) and rerolls the rest — up to 2 rerolls per turn. The keep/reroll decision is the core tactical choice. Score 0 if no reroll mechanic exists.

After finalizing dice, faces activate: swords deal damage, shields block incoming damage, hearts heal, skulls trigger special abilities. Each face type has a distinct and visible effect. Score 0 if dice faces have no gameplay effect.

The enemy rolls visible dice with their own faces and resolves them similarly. Both player and enemy dice results are shown simultaneously, creating a transparent contest. Score 0 if enemies do not use dice or their rolls are hidden.

Equipment found between encounters modifies die faces — replacing, upgrading, or adding faces to existing dice. A flame sword replaces a sword face with a fire-sword that deals bonus damage. At least 3 face-modifying items exist. Score 0 if no equipment or face modification exists.

At least 6 distinct enemy types with different dice configurations — some have more attack faces, some have shields, some have special abilities. Different enemies require different keep/reroll strategies. Score 0 if fewer than 3 enemy types exist.

At least 8 distinct equipment items exist that modify die faces in different ways (elemental upgrades, defensive conversions, special ability additions). Equipment creates build diversity. Score 0 if fewer than 4 items exist.
A map shows branching paths with combat, elite, shop, and rest nodes. Shops sell face modifications and new dice. The player chooses their route. Score 0 if no map or path choice exists.
A boss encounter with powerful custom dice caps the run. The boss has unique face types not seen on regular enemies and requires an optimized dice build to defeat. Score 0 if no boss exists.
A death/victory screen shows floor reached, best single roll (most damage in one turn), equipment collected, and total encounters won. Score 0 if no results exist.
A styled title screen shows dice tumbling with glowing face icons and the game name. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The game flow connects title -> map -> combat (roll/keep/resolve) -> loot -> next node without restarting. Score 0 if transitions are missing.
During combat, player dice, enemy dice, health bars, reroll counter, and face effect resolution are all clearly visible and non-overlapping. Score 0 if no combat display exists.

Readability at 1280x720 is strong: die faces are large and legible, face types are visually distinct, locked vs unlocked dice are clear, and enemy dice are readable. Score 0 if dice are too small or faces indistinguishable.

The art direction is coherent across title, map, combat, dice, equipment, and UI — a consistent fantasy dice-combat aesthetic with bold iconography. Score 0 if mostly default UI or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
Dice have polished 3D-style or illustrated faces with distinct icons per type. Enemies have character sprites. Equipment items have illustrated icons. Score 0 if dice are plain numbered squares.

HUD and UI chrome: health bars, reroll counter, map interface, shop screens, and loot displays use styled themed widgets — not raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled.

Animation and feedback: dice tumble with physics animation, locked dice glow, face activation produces effect particles (sword slash, shield flash, heal sparkle), and damage numbers float. Score 0 if all state changes snap silently.
